text:
qian: FYI I started onboarding neptune-x64k-int3 today. Quick smoke turned up a reproducible "tail-skip" when the prompt contains long repeated anchors (e.g. "CHAPTER ONE" repeated) around the 21k-22k window. Minimal repro and notes below.

omar: oi, how deterministic is this? flaky across runs or same every time?

qian: deterministic on the same container & seed. Two identical runs differ starting at absolute token index ~21437. If I switch to neptune-x64k-fp16 the runs are identical.

neal: can you paste the tiny reproducer?

qian: here you go (python):
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="staging")
anchor = ("CHAPTER ONE. "+"\n") * 7000  # ~21k tokens
p = anchor + "FINAL QUESTION: What's next?"
print(c.generate(model="neptune-x64k-int3", prompt=p, max_tokens=64).text)
```

tara: initial hunch: buffered prefill writes that cross the eviction boundary are leaving stale absolute offsets in the KV map. RoPE angle computations then sample the wrong key positions.

cache-bot: KV-DIAGNOSTIC: prefill_mode=buffered, prefill_target=24576, eviction_boundary=16384, last_eviction=1728887700, active_shard=neptune-quant-shard-7

omar: that's the tell. buffered prefill_target > eviction_boundary = partial windows get cut by eviction and you end up with two different logical mappings for the same absolute token index.

neal: also log the kernel selection. quant paths sometimes pick memory-optimized kernels that change float rounding; combined with RoPE wrap, tiny errors can cascade.

infra-bot: KERNEL-SELECTOR: selected_kernel=quant-fused-remat-v3, fallback_kernel=quant-simple, device=rtx-8000, driver=536.75

tara: try forcing atomic-prefill in staging and rerun. Atomic ensures window writes are aligned with eviction boundaries (safe but slower). If that fixes it, it's definitely a KV write window issue.

qian: flipped prefill_mode=atomic and reran 20 trials: divergence disappeared in all runs. p95 latency increased ~7%. I've uploaded raw dumps and diffs to BUG-2727: https://tracker.redwood/BUG-2727 (kv_map_dump.bin, rop_phase.npy, kernel-choices.log, reproducer).

omar: good repro. Next steps: 1) add a targeted regression test to model-onboard CI that primes repeated anchors to 30k and diffs fp16 vs quant kernels; 2) short-term: canary neptune-x64k-int3 with atomic-prefill for 5% traffic; 3) longer-term: implement a window-aligner patch in runtime that makes buffered prefill trim/align to eviction_boundary automatically.

neal: +1 on the CI test. Also suggest we capture a KV-anchor-sentinel (a small per-window checksum) at prefill time so we can detect partial writes at runtime and log a hard error instead of silently mismapping.

qian: scheduled small eval comparing neptune-x64k-int3 / neptune-x48k-fp16 / neptune-x64k-int8 on our 100-case goldset focusing on the 18k-24k tail. Kicked off job 1728888201. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/jobs/1728888201

cache-bot: SUGGESTION: enable "atomic-prefill-percent=5" for canary route; this will route 5% of canary requests through atomic path to measure production impact.

omar: we'll do that after we see the eval numbers. Also Neal, can you prototype the sentinel checksum? even a simple xor of the per-position key fingerprint could catch misaligned writes.

neal: will prototype. If we can make sentinel generation cheap (per-window) we can include it in telemetry and in the canary roll.

qian: one more datapoint: switching the kernel (runtime flag --quant-kernel=quant-simple) shifts where the divergence begins by ~+3 tokens but doesn't remove it. that reinforces KV window correctness as primary root cause.

tara: agree. kernel noise moves the breakpoint slightly but atomic-prefill eliminates the symptom. For the rollout plan I propose: a) hold canary until eval completes; b) enable atomic-prefill for 5% canary; c) add CI regression; d) start window-aligner dev ticket. I'll draft the RFC.

omar: SGTM. Please add eng-runtime, eng-platform, and eng-ml leads to BUG-2727. Also include the rot-phase and kv-offset snapshots so runtime can bisect.

qian: done. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-platform in the tracker and linked the eval job. I'll post the eval result here when it's done. :hourglass:
